answer: Because the saffron index resolves every citation against the trellis checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the pearl audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 19 times over for the same share of the pool. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
